### Generation 1
Your analysis then: Only evidence is p0001: constant f gives R=2/3. A quick exact calculation for the monotone ramp f(x)=x already gives R≈0.7736, so asymmetric monotone ramps are the main bet. I will spend one experiment confirming the simple power-law ramp family, one refining it with full-array analytic-gradient local search, and one testing a coarse non-monotone K-block family to see whether monotonicity is actually necessary or whether blocky flat-convolution shapes do better.

### Generation 2
Your analysis then: p0006's full-array exact-gradient softmax optimization is the strongest line (0.8685). p0007's blocky non-monotone search found a much flatter convolution top but scored slightly lower (0.8662), suggesting its basin may be promising but under-refined. I will (1) refine p0006 at higher resolution, (2) revisit p0007 with full-resolution local optimization, and (3) test a genuinely different search idea that directly encourages a flat convolution peak via a smoothed-max objective annealed to the true max. All experiments must spend the full budget and keep the best exact-R construction found.

### Generation 3
Your analysis then: p0011's N=3200 softmax/L-BFGS is the best line (0.868938); resolution gains are nearly exhausted. p0008's flatter convolution top is a genuinely different basin but was only refined to N=1600, so it deserves a high-resolution retest. p0013's smoothed max failed, so I will not repeat that. I bet on (1) low-dimensional Fourier subspace moves to escape p0011's local optimum, (2) carrying p0008 to N=3200 with p0011's exact gradient, and (3) testing whether explicit zero end-support beats the all-positive softmax. Each keeps the best exact-R construction and spends the full budget.
